programme: RFX1 driving MHC class II antigen presentation (its target list is dominated by the CIITA/HLA-DR machinery: CIITA, HLA-DRA, HLA-DMB, HLA-DOB, HLA-DPB1, HLA-E), feeding a T-cell decision node built from TOX (T-cell exhaustion/differentiation), IKZF2 (Helios; IL2RA/IL2/FOXP3-adjacent Treg identity and IL-2 signaling), NCOR2 (SMRT corepressor setting inflammatory-vs-tolerogenic balance in dendritic cells) and ZBTB16 (PLZF; innate-like T-cell and monocyte differentiation).
role_in_a: In bladder cancer this axis governs whether tumor-infiltrating T cells become exhausted/dysfunctional (TOX) versus sustain anti-tumor activity, with RFX1-driven MHC-II antigen presentation and IKZF2+ Treg activity setting how much of that T-cell response is allowed to proceed — the same axis that determines response to BCG and checkpoint immunotherapy.
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis the same node runs in the opposite direction: RFX1/MHC-II antigen presentation on the same CIITA/HLA-DR machinery that underlies the dominant MS genetic risk locus, combined with IKZF2/NCOR2-dependent failure of Treg and dendritic-cell tolerogenic restraint and ZBTB16-linked monocyte/T-cell dysregulation, permits autoreactive T cells to attack CNS myelin instead of being held in check.
shared_axis: Both diseases are failures of the same T-cell/antigen-presentation checkpoint — under-activation of tumor-reactive T cells in bladder cancer versus under-restraint of self-reactive T cells in MS — running through the shared RFX1(MHC-II)–TOX(exhaustion)–IKZF2/NCOR2(Treg-DC tolerance) machinery, with ZBTB16 marking the innate-like compartment on both sides.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally consistent (MHC-II antigen presentation feeding a T-cell exhaustion/Treg-tolerance node), and NCOR2 (3 papers) and ZBTB16 (2 papers) are independently placed in MS while TOX has a weak bladder-cancer immunotherapy hit — but RFX1, the factor that actually names the antigen-presentation anchor, has no direct paper behind it in either disease, so the connection leans on target-list interpretation and general immunology rather than retrieved co-evidence. ZBTB16 is also flagged discordant, meaning it likely contributes to the shared substrate in opposite regulatory directions rather than as an identical signal.
support: 36238311 shows SMRT/NCoR1 (NCOR2 family) tuning inflammatory vs tolerogenic dendritic-cell balance, directly relevant to autoimmune T-cell regulation; 36599367 places NCOR2 as an astrocyte regulator, giving it a CNS-relevant role; 33037402 links NCOR2/methylome regulation to vitamin D risk in MS; 42247289 shows ZBTB16-consistent T-cell/monocyte dysregulation in an MS-relevant transcriptomic study; 31064978 finds ZBTB16-linked methylation differences in MS-discordant monozygotic twins; 39545481 places IKZF2 in STAT/T-cell gene expression changes in relapsing-remitting MS; 41438430 discusses T-cell-based bladder cancer immunotherapy in a way that could implicate TOX-driven exhaustion but does not name TOX directly. No retrieved paper places RFX1 specifically in either disease; that link rests on its target composition (CIITA/HLA-DR genes), not on cited evidence.
how_to_falsify: Profile RFX1 occupancy at MHC-II loci (CIITA, HLA-DRA/DMB/DOB/DPB1) together with TOX and IKZF2/NCOR2 expression in matched tumor-infiltrating T cells from bladder tumor biopsies and in CNS/CSF- and peripheral-blood T cells and dendritic cells from MS patients. The account predicts TOX-high exhausted T cells and RFX1-driven MHC-II expression should move together in bladder tumors, and IKZF2/NCOR2-linked Treg-DC tolerogenic failure should move together with RFX1/MHC-II activity in MS. If CRISPR knockdown of RFX1 in antigen-presenting cells fails to alter MHC-II output or downstream TOX/IKZF2-associated T-cell state in either tissue, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is bladder vs. brain, so any real mechanism must be immune-cell-intrinsic (infiltrating T cells and APCs), not tissue-intrinsic — this is not a tissue-shared programme. The 650 patient-group comparisons come from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance fractions are correlated within cohort, not 650 independent replications. FOXP3 and STAT4, the canonical Treg/Th master regulators, were removed as tissue-generic, so the Treg/tolerance side of this account rests on the auxiliary factors IKZF2 and NCOR2 rather than the core Treg identity gene. ZBTB16 and ZNF217 are marked discordant between diseases; ZBTB16 is used here as a shared substrate acting in different directions, not as an identical signal, and ZNF217 was excluded from the carrying factors entirely. SETBP1 has strong bladder-cancer evidence (four papers) but its target set (HOXA10, CDKN2A, PTGS2) and lack of any MS evidence keep it outside this immune module — it looks like a separate, bladder-cancer-specific prognostic signal. NFE2, EBF2, ZNF8, HLX and ETV1 were excluded from the carrying set for lacking either disease-relevant evidence or a target profile that fits the T-cell/antigen-presentation programme. None of the single-view factors (SF1, KLF6, LMO4, MXI1, SREBF1, EN1, DNMT3B, PEG3, TFAP2C, HDGF, ESRRA, BCOR) contribute to this account.
